subject: Per-token credit & incremental commit structure for BrightAdops expansion
messages:
From: Sarah Cole <sarah@brightadops.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Matthew Stone <matthew.stone@brightadops.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Expansion pricing: new ads workload + monthly token forecast

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re close to greenlighting a new ads-serving product that will use Redwood for inference (creative gen + reranking + brand-safety embeddings). Our finance and product teams put together a conservative forecast for Q2 and wanted to get a clearer view of how you recommend structuring a pricing/commit for this new workload.

High-level:
- Expected usage: ~500M input+output tokens/month by month 3 (spread across multiple teams).
- Mix: ~60% generation, 30% embeddings, 10% reranking.
- Needs: predictable unit economics (per-token), ability to expand quickly if adoption exceeds forecast, and clear behavior for burst traffic.

Questions:
1) Do you price this via larger per-token discounts at commit tiers, or via pre-purchased credit bundles?
2) Can we do incremental commits so we don’t over-commit at the start?
3) Any packaging recommendations if multiple product teams share the same account? (billing, quotas, cost allocation)

Attached is our Q2 forecast for context (BrightAdops_forecast_Q2.xlsx). We’d love a short written proposal and a call next week to iron out the mechanics and ask Monica (pricing) questions.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Cole
Director of Product
BrightAdops

Subject: RE: Expansion pricing: new ads workload + monthly token forecast

Hi Sarah — thanks for the forecast and clear asks. Copying Monica (pricing) and Laura (acct lead) so we can align on model and timing. Below is a concise proposal we can iterate on and then formalize into a short term sheet.

Summary proposal (preview):
- Option A — Incremental commit + per-token credits (recommended for quick expansion):
  • Initial commit: 100M tokens/month for 6 months (baseline discount applied).
  • Incremental commit buckets: +100M, +200M, +500M with increasing per-token credit bonuses (see below).
  • Per-token credits: purchased credits redeemed against usage; unused credits roll forward for the commitment period.
- Option B — Tiered discounts (no upfront credits): larger committed tiers with stepped % discounts by tier.

Suggested per-token credit schedule (illustrative):
- 100M tier: base price minus 10% (or equivalent credit per 1M tokens)
- 300M cumulative: base minus 18%
- 500M+: base minus 25%

Other notes:
- Burst handling: allow a Flex pool for short-term bursts (billed at slightly higher rate or consumed from credits).
- Multi-team packaging: we recommend a single account with sub-keys + per-team billing tags. We can provide token-level billing exports so you can attribute cost back to product teams.
- SLAs and private options: dedicated or private deployments can be quoted separately if you need strict isolation.

Next steps: 1) Monica to propose firm pricing ranges and credit conversion math; 2) we share a one-page term sheet; 3) call to review and then procurement loop.

Can you do Wed 10am PT for a 30-min call?

Thanks,
Dylan

Redwood Inference

Subject: INTERNAL: pricing ranges and packaging notes for BrightAdops

Dylan / Laura — quick internal note before we lock numbers for the term sheet. Thought-through suggestions based on the forecast and our public SKU economics: 

1) Structure: Combine a small committed baseline + purchasable credits. Credits give the customer predictability while preserving unit economics for us if usage is sticky.

2) Concrete ranges (internal ranges, for alignment):
  - Baseline 100M/mo (6mo): effective discount 8–12%
  - 300M cumulative threshold: effective discount 16–20% (credits + bonus)
  - 500M+ threshold: effective discount 22–28% (requires 9–12mo commit or calendarized commit)

3) Flex pool: Bill bursts against a separate flex pool at a premium of ~+15% over committed per-token. Consider a 2x buffer for the first 30 days post-launch so their product doesn’t fail on day 1.

4) Multi-team billing: we should offer both consolidated billing + APIs to pull token usage per api-key. Recommend adding a small charge for per-team sub-accounts only if they want invoice-breakdown services.

5) Legal/procurement risks: if procurement requests data residency/SaaS-install add-ons, it will change the quote materially — flag to Sales to route to Solutions.

I’ll convert these to a simple term-sheet PDF. For now, aim to present the customer with 2 clean options (Commit+Credits vs Tiered Discount).

Monica
Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference

Sarah / Matthew — attached is a one-page proposal and an illustrative pricing table (RD-proposal-BrightAdops-v1.pdf). Highlights:

- Option 1 (Recommended): Commit+Credits
  • Initial 6-mo baseline: 100M tokens/mo at 9% off list.
  • Incremental credits: purchase in 100M buckets; credit bonus increases at 300M / 500M cumulative thresholds (equivalent to ~18% and 25% effective discounts respectively).
  • Flex pool: 50M tokens buffer billed at baseline +15% if exceeded.

- Option 2: Tiered discount only (no credits) — 12% / 19% / 26% at 100M / 300M / 500M tiers.

Operational items:
- Billing: we will provide token line-items per api-key and a monthly CSV export for cost allocation.
- Trial/rollout: propose 30-day pilot at a smaller commit, then escalate to full commit in month 2 if KPIs look good.
- Legal: propose standard MSA + SOW; we’ll route procurement/clauses through legal.

Link to term sheet: https://www.docusign.com/en/link/rd-4521-proposal

If this looks good I can generate an editable DocuSign packet for procurement. I’m available Wed 10am PT to walk through the specifics.
